content: 1. Itraconazole and Fosamprenavir/Ritonavir: Limit the itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day in patients receiving fosamprenavir/ritonavir. For patients on fosamprenavir alone, dose reductions may be necessary if itraconazole exceeds 400 mg/day. 2. Itraconazole and Fosaprepitant: Itraconazole increases fosaprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fosaprepitant may also increase itraconazole levels. Monitor closely. 3. Itraconazole and Foscarnet: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Itraconazole and Fostamatinib: Itraconazole increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to R406 (fostamatinib’s active metabolite). Monitor for toxicities and consider dose adjustments. 5. Itraconazole and Fostemsavir: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended fostemsavir doses. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Itraconazole and Futibatinib: Itraconazole increases futibatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase futibatinib toxicities. 7. Itraconazole and Ganaxolone: Minor interaction via CYP3A4 metabolism. Changes in ganaxolone exposure are not expected to be clinically significant. 8. Itraconazole and Gefitinib: Itraconazole increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Monitor closely. 9. Itraconazole and Gemifloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Itraconazole and Gemtuzumab: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Itraconazole and Gepirone: Itraconazole increases gepirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Itraconazole and Gilteritinib: Itraconazole increases gilteritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Consider alternatives to strong CYP3A4 inhibitors when co-administered with gilteritinib. 13. Itraconazole and Givinostat: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if QTc >500 ms or if there is a >60 ms change from baseline. 14. Itraconazole and Glasdegib: Itraconazole increases glasdegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Itraconazole and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Itraconazole increases levels of these drugs via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Itraconazole and Goserelin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Itraconazole and Granisetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Itraconazole and Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 19. Itraconazole and Guanfacine: Itraconazole increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose by half. No specific recommendations are available for immediate-release guanfacine. 20. Itraconazole and Haloperidol: Itraconazole increases haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Itraconazole and Histrelin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Itraconazole and Hydrocortisone: Hydrocortisone decreases itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 23. Itraconazole and Hydroxychloroquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 24. Itraconazole and Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Itraconazole increases hydroxyprogesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Itraconazole and Hydroxyzine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Itraconazole and Ibrutinib: Itraconazole increases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid concomitant use. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy. 27. Itraconazole and Ibuprofen/Famotidine: Famotidine increases gastric pH, reducing itraconazole absorption. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Administer acid-neutralizing agents at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. 28. Itraconazole and Ibutilide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Itraconazole and Idelalisib: Itraconazole increases idelalisib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for idelalisib toxicity if co-administered. 30. Itraconazole and Ifosfamide: Itraconazole decreases ifosfamide metabolism to its active metabolites via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitor closely. 31. Itraconazole and Iloperidone: Itraconazole increases iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Itraconazole and Imatinib: Itraconazole increases imatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Itraconazole and Imipramine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Itraconazole and Indacaterol: Itraconazole increases indacaterol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 35. Itraconazole and Indapamide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Itraconazole and Indinavir: Itraconazole increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce indinavir dose to 600 mg every 8 hours when co-administered. 37. Itraconazole and Inotuzumab: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Itraconazole and Irinotecan: Itraconazole increases irinotecan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 39. Itraconazole and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Itraconazole increases isavuconazonium levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Itraconazole and Isoflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Itraconazole and Isoniazid: Isoniazid decreases itraconazole levels via an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Itraconazole and Isradipine: Itraconazole increases isradipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Itraconazole and Istradefylline: Itraconazole increases istradefylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed 20 mg/day of istradefylline when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Itraconazole and Ivabradine: Itraconazole increases ivabradine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 45. Itraconazole and Ivacaftor: Itraconazole increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce ivacaftor dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Itraconazole and Ivermectin: Itraconazole increases ivermectin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Itraconazole and Ivosidenib: Itraconazole increases ivosidenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce ivosidenib dose to 250 mg daily. 48. Itraconazole and Ketamine: Itraconazole increases ketamine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 49. Itraconazole and Ketoconazole: Both drugs increase each other’s levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Itraconazole and Lacosamide: Itraconazole increases lacosamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing lacosamide dose when co-administered. 51. Itraconazole and Lansoprazole: Lansoprazole increases gastric pH, reducing itraconazole absorption. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Administer itraconazole with an acidic beverage or use the oral solution form to minimize interaction. 52. Itraconazole and Lapatinib: Itraconazole increases lapatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 53. Itraconazole and Larotrectinib: Itraconazole increases larotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce larotrectinib dose by 50% if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Itraconazole and Lefamulin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 55. Itraconazole and Lemborexant: Itraconazole increases lemborexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors.
